analysis.title: Hess Midstream LP (HESM): 3Q26 Recap: Quiet Update After CVX Restructuring; Waiting for Guidance and Further Disclosures
key_insights: HESM 3Q26 EBITDA was $320m, 2% above both GSe ($315m) and FactSet consensus ($313m). The beat came from stronger margins across segments, likely including MVC support, and lower opex.
Volumes were mostly softer than GSe: crude and gas gathering were 7% and 6% below, with gas partly reflecting planned maintenance at LM4. Water gathering was 2% above GSe.
Crude gathering and terminaling volumes both ran below 2026 MVCs, so the higher implied fees likely include MVC support.
3Q26 capex was $22m vs GSe $37m, reflecting normalization after the gas compression expansion was completed in January 2026.
2026 EBITDA guidance of $1,225-1,250m was reiterated with the release. GSe moves to $1,243m from $1,249m vs guidance midpoint $1,238m and consensus $1,242m.
The 3Q beat is more than offset by a lower 4Q26 estimate on a softer volume run-rate heading into CVX's step-down to two Bakken rigs in December.

The release carried no material updates after the early-October restructuring with sponsor Chevron (CVX). Management reiterated a YE26 close and preliminary 2027 guidance of $850-950m EBITDA and $525-625m Adj. FCF.

CVX restructuring terms: ~50% Bakken G&P rate cut, terms extended to 2045 with an 80% MRC through 2033, acquisition of CVX's DJ Basin G&P assets, a $200m cash payment to CVX, and cancellation of CVX's ~40% unit stake and its GP interest.
GS expects some incremental detail at close (guided later this quarter) and more meaningful detail with 2027 guidance early next year. Estimates do not reflect the restructuring before close.
GS acknowledges potential emerging value, as the stock implies a ~10% dividend yield, but wants more disclosure before turning constructive. Rating stays Sell.

PT cut to $29 from $33. Valuation is 7.25x (from 7.75x) on 2027 EBITDA at 85% weight plus an M&A component of 8.75x (unchanged) at 15% weight. The lower multiple reflects uncertainty about the post-close operational and financial profile.
Outer-year estimates fall ~4% on average, mostly on a softer volume outlook under the two-rig program.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $29 from $33 on a lower fundamental multiple (7.25x vs 7.75x 2027 EBITDA) given limited disclosure on the post-close profile. Price was $30.54 at the 18 Nov 2026 close, implying 5.0% downside.
CVX restructuring with HESM includes a ~50% Bakken G&P rate cut, DJ Basin G&P asset acquisition and a step-down to two Bakken rigs in December.

sector_views.rationale: HESM is rated Sell, with volume risk under CVX's two-rig program and limited disclosure on post-restructuring economics.

earnings_insights: HESM 3Q26 EBITDA reported $320m vs GSe $315m and FactSet consensus $313m, 2% above both.
2026 EBITDA guidance $1,225-1,250m reiterated. New GSe $1,243m (old $1,249m), guidance midpoint $1,238m, consensus $1,242m.

risk_factors: Upside risks to the Sell thesis: stronger contributions from the acquired DJ Basin assets including Saddlehorn, higher oil prices and thus higher CVX activity, higher-than-expected capital returns, and stronger third-party volume growth.
Limited disclosure on HESM's operational and financial profile after the CVX transaction closes.
Softer volumes under CVX's two-rig program.

tension_points.bull_case: The stock implies a ~10% dividend yield, which GS acknowledges as potential emerging value, and preliminary 2027 guidance gives $850-950m EBITDA and $525-625m Adj. FCF.
tension_points.bear_case: Disclosures on the post-close operational and financial profile remain limited, the Bakken G&P rate is cut ~50%, and volumes soften under CVX's two-rig program.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Stronger DJ Basin contributions including Saddlehorn, higher oil prices and CVX activity, higher capital returns, or stronger third-party volumes, with more disclosure at close and in 2027 guidance.
